help: Lists every planet, moon and station of a star system (default: the system you are in, or the one whose dialog is open). The header shows the stars, the number of stable locations and whether there is a gate. Each line shows: name | type | hazard | owner and size or 'unclaimed' | short summary of the conditions | ID. System names are fuzzy-matched like the 'jump' command. Unsurveyed bodies show 'unsurveyed' (the 'survey' command reveals them).

Opens the interaction dialog of any planet, moon, station or star when you close the console, from anywhere in the sector and including uncolonized planets. Names are case-insensitive; spaces or underscores both work; planet, station and market IDs work too. Example: visit Corvus_IV

Marks a colony the way Nexerelin marks colonies founded by its colony expeditions: when it grows the AI builds military and industry, Nexerelin's size limit for such colonies applies (maxNPCNewColonySize, default 6) and saturation-bombing it causes less outrage. 'off' removes the mark. If an NPC colony is already bigger than the limit you are asked to confirm first (it keeps its size but stops growing). Example: treatasnpccolony Jangala off

Caps the size of a colony: it stops growing at that size, for player and NPC colonies alike. It never shrinks a colony that is already bigger. 'off' removes the cap so it grows normally again. Prints the resulting max size. Example: popcap Jangala 5

Lists every planet type as type ID and name, grouped into habitable, hostile, gas giants and other. Includes planet types added by mods such as Unknown Skies. The optional filter only shows types whose ID or name contains that text. Example: planettypes ice

Changes the type of a planet (type ID or name, see 'planettypes'). Without 'keep' it only works on uncolonized planets: all conditions are cleared and new ones that fit the new type are rolled, and the survey status stays as it was. With 'keep' only the type changes and every condition stays; this also works on colonies. Example: terraform Corvus_IV terran

Renames a planet, moon, station or colony (the planet and its market), a whole star system, or a faction. Type the current name, then the new name: rename Glith_I Hakeball (Tab completes the current name). If you are unsure where the current name ends, put a > between the two names: rename Glith I > Hakeball. With a planet's dialog open, just type the new name: rename Hakeball. rename system <system> <new name> renames a star system together with its star and the planets named after it (Glith I becomes Hakeball I); stars follow their system's name. rename faction <faction> <new name> renames a faction everywhere ('reset' as the new name gives back its own). Everything renamed is printed.

Adds a planet orbiting the star of the system you are in, at your fleet's distance from the star and angle. Without a type (or with 'random') the type is picked at random, weighted like the sector generator. Without a name it gets the next free name like 'Corvus VI'. Its radius, orbit speed and conditions are generated like vanilla planets and it is surveyed. Refuses if the orbit would overlap the orbit of something else and says what. Example: addplanet jungle Eden

Deletes an uninhabited planet or moon, or the second or third star of a binary or trinary system, after a Yes/Cancel confirmation (or add 'yes' to confirm right away). It never picks a target by itself. Refuses main stars, colonies (use 'destroycolony' in the colony's dialog first) and bodies that moons, stations or other objects orbit, and lists them. Rings, magnetic fields, coronas and decorative orbital debris around it are removed with it, and jump points that orbit it are removed together with their hyperspace end. Example: removeplanet Corvus VI

Searches every planet and moon in the sector and lists the nearest 20 matches with type, hazard, owner, resources, distance and ID. Filters can be combined: a condition ID or group (farmland_rich, farmland, ore, ruins_vast, ruins), -condition to exclude one, habitable, uncolonized, colonized, type:<planet type>, hazard<150 (also <=, >, >=), within:<light-years from you>, owner:<faction>. Only surveyed planets and colonies are searched unless you add 'all'. Example: findplanet habitable farmland hazard<150 within:20

Shows everything about one planet, moon or station: type, size, orbit, owner, colony size and max size, popcap, NPC colony mark, industries, the hazard and how much each condition adds, all conditions and what orbits it. Unsurveyed planets keep their conditions hidden. Example: planetinfo Jangala

Lists every star type (type ID and name), grouped into normal stars, giants, dwarfs and special ones (black holes, neutron stars), including modded stars. The IDs are what newsystem and addstar take. Example: startypes giant

Adds a moon around a planet, sized and generated like vanilla moons, with rolled and surveyed conditions. If your fleet is near the planet the moon orbits at your distance, otherwise in the first free orbit. Without a name it gets the next vanilla-style name like 'Corvus IV-A'. Refuses if it would collide with other moons or rings. Example: addmoon Corvus_IV barren

Adds an asteroid belt, a dust or ice ring, or a magnetic field around the star at your distance from it, or around a named planet, using vanilla's own recipes. Refuses if it would overlap another orbit. Example: addring belt

Creates a new star system at your position in hyperspace: star (random type if none is given), light, corona, an inner and a fringe jump point plus the star's own, all reachable from hyperspace. Any star type works, including black holes (with an event horizon) and neutron stars (with a pulsar beam). A popup asks whether to generate planets, moons, rings and stable locations like a random system, or keep it empty; 'full' or 'empty' answers that in advance. The star is named '<name> Prime'. Refuses within 1.5 light-years of another system or in the Abyss. Example: newsystem Hakeball star_yellow full

Moves a planet, with everything that orbits it, to your fleet's distance and angle from what it orbits (the star, or the parent planet for moons). Refuses if the new orbit overlaps something. Objects at its L4/L5 points stay behind. Example: moveplanet Corvus_IV

Changes a planet's size. The size is its radius in the same units as orbit distances (planetinfo shows the current one): the same number changes nothing, 200% or twice the number makes it twice as wide. Vanilla rocky planets are about 90-220, gas giants 250-400; 'auto' picks a normal size for its type. Refuses if its own moons or stations would end up inside it, or if it would hit a neighbouring orbit. Examples: resizeplanet Corvus_IV 150%, resizeplanet Corvus_IV auto

Shows a faction's strength: colonies, total size, average stability, unrest, disrupted industries, garrison damage, Nexerelin invasion points and troop reserves, and any active Worldsmith effects. 'clear' ends all Worldsmith effects on that faction early. Example: factionpower hegemony

Gradually strengthens a faction. Level 1 clears unrest, repairs disrupted industries and lifts Worldsmith growth freezes. Level 2 also repairs garrisons, tops up troop reserves, adds invasion points and +2 stability for 6 months. Level 3 adds +3 stability fading by one point per year and many more invasion points. Shows a preview and asks first. Nothing is permanent. Example: strengthenfaction hegemony 2

Gradually weakens a faction. Level 1 adds unrest that fades over 6 months. Level 2 also freezes NPC colony growth for 6 months, damages garrisons, disrupts defenses for 4 months and lowers invasion points. Level 3 lasts up to 3 years: 36-month growth freeze, -3 stability fading by one point per year, military and ship industries disrupted for 1-2 years, drained troop reserves and invasion points. Shows a preview and asks first. Nothing is permanent. Example: weakenfaction hegemony 3

Explains the Worldsmith commands in plain words. Topics: names, findplanet (all filters, what within:20 or hazard<150 mean), conditions (every condition ID by group), objects, addring, resize, rename, remove, newsystem, stars, hyperspace, factions, newfaction, war, apocalypse. Example: wshelp newfaction

Removes a stable location, comm relay, nav buoy, sensor array (normal or makeshift), inactive gate, asteroid field, debris field, or a jump point made with addjumppoint (both ends) after a Yes/Cancel confirmation. Without a name it takes the nearest one where you are; with a type (stable, relay, buoy, sensor, gate, field, jumppoint) the nearest of that type; or give its name or ID. Example: removeobject field

Removes an asteroid belt (with its asteroids), a ring or a magnetic field. Without a planet it removes the one around the star that is nearest to your position; with a planet it removes all of that planet's rings, or only one kind. Never touches coronas, event horizons or pulsar beams. Example: removering Corvus_IV belt
The same as removeplanet: deletes an uninhabited moon (or planet) after a Yes/Cancel confirmation. Refuses colonies and moons that other things orbit. Example: removemoon Corvus IV-A

Adds a companion star at your position, orbiting the system's main star, which makes it a binary or trinary system: size, corona (or event horizon / pulsar beam) and light like the sector generator makes them. Refuses if it would overlap another orbit. Named '<system> B' or 'C' unless you give a name; remove it again with removeplanet. Example: addstar star_red_dwarf

Tints a planet, moon or star: red, orange, yellow, gold, green, teal, cyan, blue, purple, pink, white, grey, brown, black, a hex color like #3080ff, random, or 'reset' for its type's standard colors. Cosmetic only. Without a planet it uses the open planet dialog. Example: recolor Corvus_IV teal

In hyperspace: clears the clouds (and the storms in them) within the radius around you, or grows new clouds there. The radius is in light-years, 0.5 to 5, default 1. Star systems keep their clear space, and storms form in new clouds by themselves over time. Example: hyperclouds clear 2

Founds a new faction in one of 8 blank faction slots: its own name, a random player flag, the ships, weapons and way of fighting of an existing faction ('like <faction>' picks which one, e.g. like hegemony; otherwise a random one), empty lore, and 1, 3 or 5 colonies (small, medium, large), in your system ('here') or at a random empty place. A popup asks for whatever you leave out and shows the planets first; 'Pick another place' rolls a new random spot. Nexerelin then runs it like any other faction: diplomacy, wars, invasions, alliances. The color (red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink) picks a slot; 'spawnfaction list' shows them. A slot frees up when its faction has no colonies left. Example: spawnfaction Hakeball Republic random medium like hegemony

Changes any faction's flag (on its colonies, fleets and Intel page). Without an option a popup shows the player flags one by one as pictures (Next/Previous or the arrow keys) to pick from. Or type random, a flag number ('factionflag list'), another faction's name to copy its flag, or 'reset' for its own. Example: factionflag hegemony

Shows or rewrites a faction's lore: the text on its page in the Intel screen's faction tab. 'add' adds a paragraph, and a | inside the text starts a new paragraph, 'reset' brings back the original. Factions made with spawnfaction start with empty lore. Example: factionlore Hakeball_Republic Founded by exiles from Glith.

Shows who is at war with whom among the factions with colonies, the alliances, and how war-weary each faction is. With a faction: its relation (-100 to 100) with every other faction. For a single pair, use setrelation (Console Commands) or creatediplomacyevent <a> <b> declare_war|peace_treaty|ceasefire (Nexerelin).

Every faction with colonies goes to war with every other one, and all Nexerelin alliances break up (asks first). Your own faction stays out unless you add 'withplayer'; with a commission you share your employer's wars. Nexerelin's diplomacy can make peace again over time.

Every faction with colonies makes peace with every other one (asks first). Pirates stay hostile unless you add 'all'; 'withplayer' includes you. Wars end with Nexerelin's usual ceasefire; new wars can break out later.

Ends the world as the sector knows it, after a Yes/Cancel popup. remnant: an elite Remnant armada (alpha-core captains, no damage mods) attacks every inhabited system for about two months, then withdraws. bombard: every colony is saturation-bombed into ruins (story-critical worlds survive; can't be undone). revolution: Nexerelin rebellions break out in every colony of size 3 or more at once. Your own colonies are spared unless you add 'all'.

Adds an asteroid field or a salvageable debris field at your position, orbiting the star, like the sector generator makes them. Fields may overlap anything. Remove it again with removeobject field. Example: addfield debris large

Starts a Nexerelin rebellion in one colony (or the one whose dialog is open). The rebels fight for the faction you name, or for one Nexerelin picks from the colony's enemies, or for independence. Nexerelin runs it from there; if the rebels win, the colony changes hands. Example: rebellion Sindria persean

Sends a faction's war fleet into a star system (default: the one you are in). It arrives at a jump point, attacks the biggest colony and raids the system for about two months, then withdraws. If the two factions aren't at war, only the armada is made hostile to the colony's owner for the attack; no war is declared. Example: armada hegemony Askonia large

Places a vanilla object at your position, orbiting the star: stable_location, comm_relay, nav_buoy, sensor_array, their makeshift versions, or inactive_gate. Relays, buoys and arrays start unclaimed. Refuses if the orbit overlaps something. Remove it with removeobject. Example: addobject comm_relay

Adds a two-way jump point where your fleet is. In a star system: a jump point at your position, with its other end in hyperspace just outside the system. In hyperspace: a jump point here into the nearest system (up to 3 light-years away), arriving at that system's edge. Remove both ends with removeobject jumppoint. Example: addjumppoint Back Door

For a faction made with spawnfaction: which ships its new fleets use. lowtech, midline or hightech keep only ships of that tech, pirate uses pirate and low tech hulls, all uses every ship the sector's factions use, and 'like <faction>' copies another faction completely: the same ships, the same weapons and the same way of fighting (e.g. like tritachyon makes it fly Tri-Tachyon ships with Tri-Tachyon tactics). Without an option it shows the current setting. Example: factionships Hakeball_Republic hightech

For a faction made with spawnfaction: how its fleets are built and fight. aggressive or cautious; carriers, phase or warships; elite (few, top-quality ships and officers) or swarm (many cheap ships); capitals (big ships). Presets stack, and one that sets the same thing replaces the other; reset goes back to its model faction. Without an option it shows the doctrine. Example: factiondoctrine Hakeball_Republic carriers

For a faction made with spawnfaction: how it behaves. warlike (declares war easily, tires of it slowly) or peaceful (never starts wars itself); pirate (Nexerelin treats it as a pirate faction: hostile to everyone but pirates, free ports, nothing illegal) or lawful (back to normal diplomacy); expansionist (sends colony expeditions often) or isolationist (none); normal resets all of it. Without an option it shows the current personality. Example: factionpersonality Hakeball_Republic pirate
